review_notes: I read the whole target file (408 lines) and checked the definitions and results it depends on: `TauCeti.SolidTorus` (SeifertFibration.lean:77), `TauCeti.normalSubspace`/`normalTube`/`mem_normalTube` and `exists_isOpenEmbedding_normalTube` (Geometry/Manifold/TubularNeighborhood/Euclidean.lean), `deriv_comp_circleExp_ne_zero_and_range_mfderiv` (Geometry/Manifold/Instances/Sphere.lean:245), `cross_orthonormal` (Geometry/Euclidean/Angle/Unoriented/CrossProduct.lean:36), and the downstream users in SolidTorusNeighborhood/Exterior.lean and Sphere.lean. I checked the vacuity-sensitive items specifically: `SolidTorus.closure_setOf_norm_lt_one` (open solid torus is indeed dense in `D² × S¹`), `IsSolidTorusNeighborhood.frontier_image` (correct: closure of the open solid torus is univ, the closed embedding gives `closure (Φ '' s) = Φ '' closure s`, injectivity gives the sdiff, and `{‖w‖ ≤ 1} \ {‖w‖ < 1} = {‖w‖ = 1}`), `exteriorFrontierHomeomorph` (codomain is `frontier ((Φ '' open)ᶜ)`, matching `frontier_compl`), the frame lemmas (`n₁ z`, `n₂ z` do lie in the normal space and span it, derivable from the stated decomposition iff plus orthonormality), and `exists_isSolidTorusNeighborhood` (the hypotheses `C²` + injective `mfderiv` + injective `f` match the documented 'C² embedded circle'; the statement is inhabited by the standard embedded circle). I also considered but did not report: `exists_forall_notMem_span_tangentVector`'s hypothesis `2 < Module.finrank ℝ V` is automatically false in infinite-dimensional `V`, while its docstring says 'a space of dimension at least three'; since the lemma is private, used only at `V = ℝ³`, and Mathlib's Sard lemma needs the `finrank` formulation, I could not establish that the generality loss is unintentional rather than a deliberate formalization choice, so I did not raise it. The one justified finding is the docstring/statement mismatch in `exists_normalDisc`, whose documented 'linear isometries' are not part of the conclusion (norm preservation plus bijectivity onto the normal space does not determine linearity).

findings.problem: The docstring promises 'a continuous family of linear isometries `ψ z : ℂ → ℝ³` onto its normal planes', but the conclusion contains no linearity at all: it only says `ψ z` lands in the normal subspace, preserves norms, is injective, and is surjective onto the normal subspace. These conditions do not determine the map up to linearity. Concretely, if `ψ` satisfies the stated conclusion and `φ : ℂ → ℂ` is any norm-preserving bijection that is not ℝ-linear (e.g. `w ↦ w * exp(‖w‖ ^ 2 * Complex.I)`, which rotates each circle by a radius-dependent angle and fixes `0`), then `ψ' z w = ψ z (φ w)` still satisfies every clause of the statement (continuity, normal-space membership, `‖ψ' z w‖ = ‖w‖`, injectivity, surjectivity) but is not linear, so the stated lemma does not separate the intended linear isometries from arbitrary non-linear norm-preserving maps. The module docstring (lines 35–36) advertises this step as trivializing the normal bundle, but the statement gives no additivity or scalar-multiplication fact, so a reader cannot obtain `ψ z (w + w') = ψ z w + ψ z w'` or a linear equivalence `ℂ ≃ₗ[ℝ] normalSubspace`. This is a missing conclusion relative to the documented purpose, not a false statement: the actual construction `fun z w => w.re • n₁ z + w.im • n₂ z` (line 339) is ℝ-linear, so the stronger claim is what is really proved.
findings.proposed_change: State the result with a linear-isometry-valued family, e.g. `∃ ψ : Circle → ℂ →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³, Continuous (fun q : SolidTorus => ψ q.2 q.1) ∧ ∀ z, range (ψ z) = normalSubspace (𝓡 1) f z` (norm preservation, injectivity and surjectivity then follow from the linear isometry structure and the range equality), or, if the bundled form is inconvenient, add the linearity clauses `ψ z 0 = 0`, `ψ z (w + w') = ψ z w + ψ z w'`, `ψ z (c • w) = c • ψ z w` together with `∀ v ∈ normalSubspace (𝓡 1) f z, ∃ w, ψ z w = v`. The existing construction `w.re • n₁ z + w.im • n₂ z` should still supply the proof, using the orthonormality facts already extracted from `exists_normalFrame`.
findings.benefit: The lemma would then actually state the normal-bundle trivialization the file advertises: downstream proofs (and readers) could use linearity to rewrite sums and real scalar multiples of normal vectors, and the docstring would no longer claim more than the theorem delivers. Packaging `ψ z` as a `ℂ →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³` also removes the redundant-looking `Injective`/`‖ψ z w‖ = ‖w‖`/surjectivity combination in favour of a single standard structure.
